divergence: connection close on a close-delimited body
scenarios.divergence: net/http deletes a Connection header carrying close, and a close-delimited body closes either way, so the port cannot tell the header was there: pi's record has connection: close, the port's does not

scenarios.name: divergence: a trailer named in lowercase
scenarios.divergence: net/http moves the Trailer header into Response.Trailer under canonical names, so the port's record has trailer: X-T where pi's keeps the text sent, x-t

scenarios.name: divergence: a connection header holding more than close
scenarios.divergence: net/http deletes a whole HTTP/1.1 Connection header once it holds a close token, in any case, keeping only resp.Close, so the port's record has the lone connection: close it can infer where pi's keeps the header as sent, keep-alive, Close

scenarios.name: divergence: trailer names out of order
scenarios.divergence: net/http moves the Trailer header into Response.Trailer, a map, so the port's record lists the names sorted, X-A, X-B, where pi's keeps them as sent, X-B, X-A (their case and repeated lines are lost too)

scenarios.name: divergence: a transfer-encoding sent in another case
scenarios.divergence: net/http consumes Transfer-Encoding and keeps only that the body is chunked, so the port's record has transfer-encoding: chunked where pi's keeps the text sent, Chunked

scenarios.name: divergence: a repeated content-length
scenarios.divergence: undici rejects a response with two Content-Length lines, even equal ones, and pi fails with fetch failed; net/http merges equal ones into one and the port reads the body to done

scenarios.name: divergence: a brotli body the caller asked for
